jobs.description: FACILITIES MANAGER EUROPE (F/M/D)At Clario, part of Thermo Fisher Scientific, we develop regulated technology that helps unlock better evidence and improve patient outcomes worldwide. Our software platforms support clinical trials, diagnostics, and medical decision?making in highly controlled regulatory environments.As Facilities Manager Europe (f/m/d), you will support Clario's facilities across Europe with a focus on our office in Estenfeld, Germany.WHAT WE OFFER*Competitive compensation.*Flexible working hours and working time accounts to support the work-life balance.*Hybrid work model, allowing for 1-2 days of remote work after the probation period.*Support your professional development through internal and external training and certification programs.*Attractive benefits (security, flexibility, support and well-being).*Engaging employee programs.WHAT YOU´LL BE DOING*Facilities Operations: Providing overall facilities support by ensuring the seamless delivery of facility operations, building management, structural measures, maintenance teams, housekeeping, reception, cafeteria operations, asset management, visitor management, and security & safety protocols. Clario's primary European facilities are situated in Germany, Hungary, Belgium, Switzerland, and Turkey.*Facility Layout Standards and Compliance: Supporting facility layout standards for electrical systems, HVAC, IT infrastructure (phones, conference systems, displays), materials, access control and more. Collaborating with local contractors/vendors/departments to manage these processes through to completion, ensuring compliance with local and state building codes.*Site Coordination: Managing and coordinating the logistics involved in opening, relocating, or closing a facility, including security systems, access control, furniture, signage, showroom/marketing requirements, telecommunications, and more.*Budgeting and Capital Expenditure: Actively participating in the capital expenditure budgeting process and managing purchasing requests for facility needs. Accurately forecasting and preparing facility-related budgets. Conducting financial and business analysis, including preparing reports on expenditures, savings, and areas for cost optimization.*Compliance and Standards Development: Ensuring all facilities are operated and maintained in compliance with local, state, and national laws, company standards, and procedures. Responsible for developing and refining standards as business needs evolve, including ensuring annual occupational safety and fire inspections where applicable.*Stakeholder and Management Communication: Maintaining a dotted line to the local management teams, participating in and reporting at management meetings. Building strong relationships with key business stakeholders by collecting feedback and delivering reports on business-critical aspects, such as occupancy, site launches, and facility improvements and audits.*External Relations and First Point of Contact: Serving as the First Point of Contact for the landlord, labor inspectorate, municipalities, authorities, and occupational safety departments.*Vendor and Contractor Management: Building and maintaining strong relationships with local building management and managing third-party contractors/vendors responsible for facility maintenance and operations. This includes monitoring tasks completed, overseeing technical acceptance, and approving invoices.*Lease and Contract Management: Managing leases and facility agreements, including understanding legal terms and commercial contract structures. Ensuring contracts are renewed and negotiated in a timely manner.*Sustainability and Energy Efficiency: Supporting sustainability initiatives by tracking, reporting, and working towards reducing emissions and waste across facility operations. Implementing energy-saving initiatives, including tracking energy consumption and suggesting areas for improvement.*Crisis and Emergency Management: Developing and maintaining emergency response plans for the facility, including fire drills, evacuation procedures, and pandemic-related safety measures.*Training and Development: Coordinating safety and facility-related training for employees to ensure everyone is aware of evacuation procedures, safety protocols, and proper usage of shared resources like conference rooms, equipment, and storage areas.*Team Collaboration and Support: Contributing to team success by assisting colleagues in resolving internal issues and supporting shared goals.*Quality and Standards Management: Ensuring adherence to organizational SOPs by regularly reviewing and understanding operational guidelines. Supporting the establishment and enforcement of departmental standards to maintain consistent quality service.*Technical and Industry Development: Enhancing expertise through active participation in company-sponsored training programs and maintaining up-to-date knowledge of industry trends and emerging technologies to drive innovation and informed decision-making.WHAT WE LOOK FOR*Bachelor’s degree in Facility Management or a comparable degree with a technical background, alongside additional business management training or further development.*Five or more years of experience in facilities management or an equivalent role, including proven experience in managing technical building projects.*Fluent language skills in both German and English are required. Additional language skills are beneficial.*Organizational and time management skills to prioritize tasks and meet established schedules, timelines, or deadlines.*Creative problem-solving skills with strong project management abilities.*Proficiency in working with computer software, including the MS Office suite.*Ability to influence others without direct authority.*Strong ability to adapt to changing priorities.*A strong desire to succeed while maintaining a professional and positive attitude.*Flexibility to travel to our European sites as needed, typically averaging two trips per year.At Clario, our purpose is to transform lives by unlocking better evidence. It’s a cause that unites and inspires us. It’s why we come to work—and how we empower our people to make a positive impact every day. Whether you're advancing clinical science, building innovative technology, or supporting our global teams, your work helps bring life-changing therapies to patients faster.AnsprechpartnerSebastian BraunJetzt bewerben [https://clarioclinical.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/clarioclinical_careers/details/Facilities-Manager-Europe--f-m-d-_R17628]

RoleHive Robotics builds RF communication and orchestration systems for unmanned platforms: connecting, controlling and commanding multi-vendor drone and robot swarms. Our systems are made in Germany, in serial production and deployed on active frontlines.You’ll be our first sales hire. There is no sales team, no SDRs and no playbook to inherit. This is a hands-on role: you find the leads, make the calls, write the offers and negotiate the contracts yourself. You work directly with our founders, report to the CEO, and get a lot of trust and room to decide how you sell. We measure you on signed contracts.Some leads come from our founders and Business Development. Many you’ll find yourself, through cold calls, cold emails, events and your own network. You take over a live pipeline and our existing customers, so we expect your first closes within three months.You don’t need a defence background or an engineering degree. Our engineers and Field Application Engineers know the product in depth, and you can bring them in whenever a deal needs it. What we need from you is the ability to run large, complex deals to signature on your own.Responsibilities- Close deals. Take opportunities from the first conversation to a signed contract, negotiate price and terms yourself, and bring in the founders when a deal needs them.- Build your own pipeline. Leads from the founders and BD give you a start. The rest comes from your own outreach: cold calls, emails, LinkedIn, trade fairs and introductions you find yourself.- Grow our existing customers through follow-on orders, new units and new use cases.- Write the offer: configuration and pricing, terms, the business case on the customer’s own numbers and the plan to signature. Handle tenders and RFPs where they apply.- Use trials to win contracts. Before a trial starts, scope, success criteria, pilot price and the path to the main contract are agreed in writing. Operations handles the paperwork.- Keep a forecast the founders can plan with: disciplined qualification, an up-to-date CRM and a short weekly pipeline review.- Set up the tools you work with every day, from offer templates to your CRM.RequirementsWhat you bring- 5 to 10 years in B2B sales, ideally around 7, with a clear record of closing- Deals of €2m to €10m and more that you personally negotiated and closed- Experience with buyers who decide in groups: users, technical teams, procurement, legal and management- You do the work yourself. You research accounts, pick up the phone and write your own offers, without a team preparing things for you.- Closing is what drives you. You chase the next step, follow up until you get an answer and don’t let deals stall.- You write down offers, decisions and customer commitments, so Operations and the founders can act on them without asking- Willingness to travel 30-50%, mostly within Germany and Europe, sometimes further- Fluent English; German is a strong plus- Eligibility and willingness to undergo security vetting, which some customer sites requireNice to have- Experience selling hardware or other physical products with lead times and delivery commitments- Experience with defence, public-sector or other long, regulated buying processes- You’ve worked as the first or only salesperson in a company beforeFurther InformationYou start with a solid base salary that gives you a stable foundation. On top of that comes a strong variable component tied directly to the deals you close: the more you close, the more you earn, and strong performers earn well above their base. You also participate in Hive through our VSOP, so you share in the value you help build.Über unsWe work in deep-tech and dual-use technology, an industry where women and other underrepresented groups have historically had limited access. We encourage you to apply even if you don't check every box below.Why Hive- Build sovereign technology that matters. We build RF communication and orchestration systems for unmanned platforms across air, land, sea, and space, at a moment when European technological sovereignty is a real strategic question, not an abstract one.- Real ownership, real deployment. Our products are already in serial production and in the field. What you build ships, and you see the result.- Small team, direct access. Around 30 people. You'll work directly with founders and not through multiple layers of management.- You shape the foundations. We're still building the structures, career paths, controlling, compliance, that let a fast-growing company scale well. You'll help decide what they look like.- Modern Munich office, with the tools and equipment to do your best work.What You Get- **Compensation. **We benchmark salaries to stay competitive for the market and the role, not just what an early-stage budget can spare.- Equity. You participate in Hive through equity/VSOP, a genuine stake in what we build, not just a paycheck.- A role you shape, not one you're handed. We're too early for fixed job descriptions or a career ladder. What you own grows as you take on more, not by climbing steps someone else defined.- No bureaucracy. Small, flat team. Decisions happen in a conversation, not a sign-off chain.Compensation and equity terms vary by role and level.Hive Robotics is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications regardless of race, ethnic origin, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, or marital status. Build Europe's semiconductor future with us!Join us to build up one of Europe’s most advanced semiconductor manufacturing sites in Dresden.As a Quality Control Technician you serve as the final quality gate before our products reach global customers.In this role, you combine automated optical inspection (AVI), systematic defect review, and final documentation checks in a cutting-edge cleanroom facility. During your onboarding starting in February 2027, you will complete a 6-month training program in Taiwan to gain hands-on fab experience, master core inspection procedures, and build a strong international network.Job Responsibilities• Operate optical inspection tools and manage Automated Visual Inspection recipes.• Perform detailed defect reviews, verify hold lots, and generate structured defect reports for engineering evaluation.• Validate outgoing wafer documentation and ensure strict compliance with quality, handling, and shipping standards.• Execute cleanroom environmental monitoring and support routine tool calibration and 6S audit processes.• Conduct initial troubleshooting on inspection equipment and execute lot disposition according to standard procedures.• Manage operational inventory of cleanroom parts, consumables, and Front Opening Shipping Boxes.• Handle manual packing and safe dispatch preparation of finished goods for warehouse transfer.• Work in rotating shift schedules (initially a 2-shift model, transitioning to a continuous 5-crew 3-shift roster).Your profile Must Have:• Completed technical vocational training (Berufsausbildung) or equivalent with technical background/aptitude.• Hands-on experience in manufacturing, production, or quality inspection environments. Semiconductor experience is a plus, but motivated entry-level candidates and cross-industry applicants are welcome).• Willingness to work in a cleanroom environment (90%), covering physical material handling as well as stationary desk-based analysis.• Readiness to work rotating shifts.• Solid PC literacy (MS Office, especially Excel).• Professional English proficiency (min. B2) and at least basic German language skills.• Availability for onboarding in February 2027, including the 6-month training in Tainan, Taiwan.Nice to Have:• Prior experience in cleanroom environments, semiconductor manufacturing, or precision industries (e.g., optics, electronics, medical technology).• Basic understanding of defect inspection systems, statistical process control, or 6S principles.• Mandarin language skills (beneficial for cross-site collaboration).Reasons to join ESMC• Security & Perspective: A permanent employment contract and career advancement opportunities in one of Europe's leading semiconductors fabs.• Company Pension Plan & Financial Benefits: We support your financial well-being with our robust company pension plan. As an ESMC employee, you also benefit directly from TSMC’s performance through an exclusive Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP).• Relocation Support for Dresden: Moving for us? We’ll provide you with all the support you will need for your relocation and your start in Dresden.• Training & Development: At the TSMC Newcomer Training Center, gain a deeper understanding of the processes involved in operating complex semiconductor equipment through unique hands-on training, while you continuously expand your knowledge.• Health & Well-Being: An annual budget for your health and well-being (e.g., for sports classes, massages, or relaxation) helps you stay fit.• Meals & Transportation: Enjoy a daily meal allowance as well as a subsidized public transportation (e.g., for the Deutschlandticket).Application documentsPlease apply with your English CV.About usEach journey starts with a first step.Joining ESMC at this early stage will provide you with the unique opportunity to actively shape the future of the fab in Dresden, boost your career and put your true potential to the test.
